reasoning: Owned PPE is small (NBV 4,455 at 31.12.2025; gross 24,427, mostly satellite comms equipment on 7-year lives, computers 3 years). PPE depreciation ran 1,776-2,130 a year in 2023-25 and capex averaged 2,037 over 2021-25, so ~2.0-2.1m USD a year keeps the owned network whole.
2023-24 capex (3,082 and 2,529) was above depreciation because of the Israel ISP build-out (directors' report FY2023 p.86) - treat the excess as growth. 2025 capex (1,362) was below depreciation.

H1 2026 capex jumped to 7,828k ILS (~2.5m USD at ~3.1) for communication equipment on new government/integration projects; if this persists, maintenance may be nearer the high case. The consolidated H1 note that would split PPE vs intangibles is not in the supplied PDF.

The economic network (satellite transponders, fibre segments) is leased, not owned: lease principal + interest was 11,309 USD in 2025 (36,537k ILS TTM) plus 11,550 of short-term leases already in cost of revenue. Per fund rule these are operating costs, not capex: do not add back ROU depreciation, deduct lease principal.

Bezeq IRU prepayments (3,902 USD in 2025; 10,019k ILS in H1 2026) run through operating cash flow as 'deferred expenses'. They buy fibre-line rights ahead of ISP subscriber growth, so the amount above the yearly amortisation (1,079 in 2025) is growth spend; the amortisation is the steady-state cost and must stay deducted (company EBITDA and 'FCF excl. prepaid' add it back). Under the Nov 2025 addendum, up to ~160m ILS for 36,000 more lines over 3 years (plus 3 x ~80m ILS tranches in 2029/31/33, each conditional on growth targets) is still to come, payable over up to 10 annual instalments with interest.
Customer-relationship amortisation (809 a year) comes from an old acquisition and needs no cash replacement; it is not maintenance capex.
